g.text: What we store, and for how long
Postgres serves inside the fresh TTL.
Past the TTL, the waterfall runs.
The first complete answer is stored.
All layers fail: the stored value
is served up to max stale,
delta fetch after the last stored key
raw close, dividends, splits, Form 4, filings, 13F
New rows, plus a known revised window
GDP, payrolls, adjusted CPI, trade flows, factors
One current value that can change
refetch after the TTL, keep dated versions
profile, peers, issuer holdings, next earnings
An adjusted close changes after each later dividend or split.
A raw close never changes. So we store the raw close plus
the corporate actions, and compute adjClose on read.
Past price rows never need a rewrite.
A delta from a different layer refetches the last stored day.
If the closes differ by more than 0.5 %, the full window
reloads from the new layer. Layers are never mixed.
WHAT WE MAY STORE AND SHOW
SEC EDGAR, US Treasury, BLS, BEA, EIA, NY Fed, NBER, OpenFIGI
World Bank (CC BY 4.0), OECD, IMF, Kenneth French, Shiller
Alpaca, Tiingo, Finnhub, Yahoo, Alpha Vantage, UN Comtrade
History is the asset. It must
Delta fetch asks for the last date
Caffeine keeps hot reads in memory,
so most reads skip the database.
